cohort: The study included 619 mother-neonate pairs delivered at Saad Abuelela Maternity Hospital in Sudan.
finding: Multivariate analysis revealed that cesarean delivery, preterm delivery, and low birth weight were significantly associated with an increased odds of perinatal asphyxia.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was identified as an independent risk factor for perinatal asphyxia, with an adjusted odds ratio of 2.31.
cross-section timing: At birth/immediate neonatal period within the hospital setting
birth_weight: N/A (low birth weight was identified as a risk factor, but the overall birth weight range of the cohort is not specified)
gest_age: N/A (preterm delivery was identified as a risk factor, but the overall gestational age range of the cohort is not specified)
